Topics. AI discoverability / the "Found" stage, ensuring the robots.txt file does not block AI agents (e.g., testing with curl -A ClaudeBot), avoiding JavaScript-dependent content rendering that hides text from crawlers, implementing proper schema markup for structured product data; the Shopify Global Product Catalog / enabling the Agentyc storefront requirement to allow inclusion in backend AI product catalogs (bypassing open-web scraping); AI keyword matching / the "Matched" stage, replacing fluffy marketing copy with hard, specific data facts (e.g., container size, exact colors, exact use cases) so AI can filter the product into the top 100 candidates; AI recommendation logic / the "Chosen" stage, recognizing that final AI recommendations rely on off-page reputation and social proof (external reviews on platforms like Reddit), similar to traditional backlink authority.

Look for.

The JavaScript Readability Check: The recommendation to disable JavaScript in the browser and reload the page to see exactly what an AI crawler sees, ensuring that critical content (like reviews or FAQs) isn't hidden behind delayed app widgets.

The Global Catalog Check: The specific tip to use Shopify's "Sidekick" AI assistant to verify if a store's products are eligible for the Shopify global product catalog, which feeds independent AI shopping tools.

Explicit Fact Matching: The shift in product description copywriting from vague, fluffy marketing language (e.g., "perfect for life on the go") to explicit, factual keywords (e.g., "insulated water bottle, green, cold drinks") because AI relies on exact data points to build shortlists.

Skip. Promotional pitches for the developer bootcamp or ideas for how developers can charge clients for audits.

Scope mix. 100% growth (advanced strategies for AI search adaptation).

Volume. ~250 words.

Topics. seo analytics / Evaluating high-level search performance using Google Search Console metrics (clicks, impressions, CTR, average position). Isolating true organic growth by filtering out branded search terms using Custom Regex (doesn't match combined with pipe symbols for "or"). Identifying content gaps and new content opportunities by exporting Search Console query data to find terms the site surfaces for without dedicated coverage. rank tracking / Monitoring page and keyword positioning over time without paid rank trackers by filtering performance reports by exact query or specific URLs, and using comparison modes to measure rank shifts. Tracking emerging AI-driven search presence through Google's generative AI performance report (covering AI Overviews and AI mode impressions). site auditing / Troubleshooting indexation issues via the URL inspection tool and pages report. Differentiating between "Discovered - currently not indexed" (Google knows the page exists but hasn't crawled yet) and "Crawled - currently not indexed" (Google read the page and passed due to thin or duplicate content signals). Checking video indexing rules (ensuring videos live on dedicated "watch pages" rather than embedded halfway down a post) and reviewing baseline backlink and internal linking reports.

Look for. The definition of "Discovered - currently not indexed": Google knows the page exists but hasn't crawled it yet. The definition of "Crawled - currently not indexed": Google read the page and chose to pass on it, usually indicating content quality or thinness issues. The specific regex method to filter out branded terms: using doesn't match with brand terms separated by a pipe symbol (|). The rule for Google video indexing: the video must be the main event of the page on a dedicated "watch page."

Skip. Promotional walkthroughs for signing up for or configuring third-party content optimization tools like Surfer. General introductory overviews of Google Search Console's dashboard navigation.

Scope mix. Almost all baseline.

Volume. 15 to 20.

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides a structured, three-step approach to SEO (identifying keywords/intent, building E-E-A-T compliant pages, and powering them up via topical clusters and internal links) that debunks "guaranteed ranking" myths. modules: [SEO] topics: [search intent, E-E-A-T, topical authority, internal linking, keyword targeting, backlinking] tier: 2 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. keyword targeting / selecting core business-driving keywords (brand name, explicit product names, specific services) instead of trying to rank for everything; search intent / analyzing the SERP (Search Engine Results Page) to understand Google's "assumed search intent," identifying mixed intent queries (e.g., homepages vs. listicles vs. Reddit discussions), and adapting formatting (e.g., using a roundup post backdoor when out-branded by enterprise competitors); E-E-A-T / optimizing content to demonstrate Experience (original photos, screenshots, case studies, personal anecdotes) and Accountability (author bylines, publish dates), moving beyond simple word counts to comprehensive factual coverage; topical authority / building an ecosystem of related, interconnected content pieces around a central topic (rather than relying on a single isolated post) to signal expertise to search engines; internal linking / using supporting blog posts to earn natural backlinks (e.g., informative guides) and then passing that link authority (link juice) directly to the bottom-funnel money pages (e.g., product/sales pages) via contextual internal links.

Look for.

The SERP Intent Check: Googling a target keyword before writing to see what format Google ranks (e.g., if the top 5 results are homepages, target your homepage; if the top results are listicles, build a listicle).

The Roundup Post Backdoor: The strategy of creating an objective "best of" listicle that features competitors alongside your own product, used to rank for highly competitive software/product keywords when your domain lacks the authority to rank its homepage.

The E-E-A-T "Experience" Mandate: Proving first-hand experience by utilizing original photography, actual screenshots of software dashboards, and author bylines, specifically avoiding generic AI-spun fluff.

The Link Authority Transfer: The specific tactic of earning backlinks to top-of-funnel educational blog posts (which are easier to get links for than sales pages), and then internally linking those posts to the bottom-funnel money pages to transfer the SEO power.

Skip. Promotional pitches for the Surfer software tool and generic disclaimers about not guaranteeing #1 rankings.

Scope mix. 100% baseline (standard SEO execution and strategy). Volume. ~350 words.

Topics. search intent / differentiating between informational, commercial, transactional, and navigational intent, evaluating the SERP (Search Engine Results Page) to determine Google's classification; keyword research / utilizing the Keyword Sweet Spot framework (demand, fit, intent, difficulty), prioritizing longtail keywords to target highly focused intent with lower competition; keyword clustering / grouping topically related keywords to build "Topical Authority," ensuring the website covers the full customer journey rather than scattering topics; prioritization / starting with bottom-funnel "money pages" (conversion-focused product or service pages) before creating top-funnel educational blogs, connecting top-funnel content to money pages via internal linking; content creation / leveraging AI for structure/outlines but mandating human differentiation (expert insights, original data, specific examples, real opinions) to beat AI-spun slop; on-page SEO / technical execution including H1 title tags, keyword-rich and concise URLs, meta descriptions, alt-text for images, and internal linking; link building / emphasizing organic linkable assets (free tools, calculators, comprehensive guides) and using PR platforms (Source of Sources / HARO) to earn high-authority citations; AI Search (GEO) / optimizing for chatbots (ChatGPT, Perplexity) by creating comprehensive, structured content and earning citations on authoritative third-party sites, as AI LLMs heavily weight frequently cited sources.

Look for.

The Intent Check: Searching a target keyword in Google and explicitly analyzing the top 10 ranking pages. If the top 10 are all comparison blogs, the intent is commercial. If the top 10 are product pages, the intent is transactional.

The "Money Page First" Rule: Building the bottom-funnel conversion pages (product/pricing pages) before writing any informational blog content, ensuring top-of-funnel traffic has a destination to convert.

Cluster Construction: Writing 5-10 interconnected articles on a single narrow topic (e.g., coffee brewing ratios) to establish "Topical Authority" before moving on to an entirely different subject (e.g., sales forecasting).

Human Content Moats: Manually inserting original data, case studies, proprietary expertise, and strong opinions into AI-generated drafts to prevent the content from failing against the 96% of web pages that receive zero traffic.

The Generative Search Loop: Understanding that AI assistants (like ChatGPT) use traditional search indexes (like Bing) to retrieve answers, meaning traditional SEO indexing and third-party citations remain the foundation for appearing in AI answers.

Skip. Plugs for the Surfer software tool and generic explanations of what Google is.

Scope mix. 20% baseline (basic definition of intent and URLs), 80% growth (Topical Authority clustering, GEO, and link-building tactics). Volume. ~400 words.

06-MEA / measurement and analytics

Goes here. SEO tracking, search engine analytics, rank tracking, tracking organic search performance, monitoring technical site health (site audits), analyzing keyword performance, backlink profile tracking, competitor keyword gap analysis, and tracking AI visibility/AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) benchmarks across LLMs.

Not here.

Paid advertising performance, ROAS, or attribution -> 06-MEA (other sub-topics) or 11-ADC

Writing and executing optimized blog content or copy -> 10-MCR

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details how to use Semrush One to measure organic search performance, track keyword rankings and AI visibility (AEO) across platforms like ChatGPT and Perplexity, conduct site health audits, and analyse backlink gaps. modules: [MEA] topics: [seo analytics, rank tracking, site auditing] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. seo analytics / Measuring search performance by analyzing keyword volume, search intent (Informational, Navigational, Commercial, Transactional), and Keyword Difficulty (KD). Performing keyword gap and backlink gap analyses against competitors to discover missing ranking opportunities and high-authority link-building targets (like the Food Network). Utilizing topic research tools to discover trending headlines and user questions to build out content planning queues. rank tracking / Monitoring Google search positions and AI visibility over time using Semrush Position Tracking and Domain Overview. Differentiating between traditional SEO rank tracking and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) tracking, which measures how brands appear in AI-generated answers and LLM outputs (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Gemini). Utilizing the AI Visibility toolkit and Brand Performance reports to track LLM sentiment, share of voice, key business drivers, and strategic recommendations. site auditing / Executing technical site health checks using the Semrush Site Audit tool to identify and prioritize critical errors (like 404 broken links returning 4XX status codes) versus warnings. Ensuring site crawlability for both traditional search engines (via robots.txt) and AI bots/LLMs (via llms.txt files).

Look for. The definition of KD (Keyword Difficulty): a percentage metric showing how hard it is to rank for a keyword. The four search intent types: Informational (I), Navigational (N), Commercial (C), and Transactional (T). The definition of AEO (Answer Engine Optimization): the practice of optimizing content to appear in AI-generated search answers and LLM chats. The two critical text files for crawlability: robots.txt for Google and llms.txt for AI tools.

Skip. Promotional walkthroughs for signing up for the Semrush 14-day free trial or entering credit card details. The conceptual description of the Semrush One platform UI sidebar layout.

Scope mix. Almost all baseline.

15-SEO / search engine optimization Goes here. A complete Shopify SEO guide covering keyword research (using Google Keyword Planner and Trends), on-page optimization for homepages, product pages, and collections (editing the Title, Meta Description, URL handle, and H1 tags), generating alt-text for images, creating SEO-optimized product descriptions, handling 301 redirects, mobile-friendliness checks, adding Rich Snippets (Schema markup), and submitting XML sitemaps to Google Search Console. Not here. • Configuring backend settings like shipping or taxes -> 05-SET • The visual design of a product page without an SEO focus -> 07-LPG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the step-by-step process for executing on-page SEO within the Shopify backend, from extracting high-intent keywords to editing the "Search Engine Listing" fields and implementing 301 redirects. modules: [SEO] topics: [keyword research, on-page SEO, title tags, meta descriptions, image optimization, rich snippets, XML sitemaps] tier: 2 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. keyword research / using Google Keyword Planner to find main and supporting keywords, evaluating search volume and CPC, using Google Trends to find related queries, analyzing competitor URLs; intent / differentiating between informational intent ("how to make homemade soap") and transactional intent ("homemade soap near me" or "homemade soap for sale"); global SEO settings / editing the homepage Title and Meta Description via Online Store > Preferences; on-page SEO / ensuring only one H1 tag exists per page, using ChatGPT to rewrite product titles and generate 100+ word descriptions based on specs; image optimization / compressing files before upload (keeping them under 2MB), writing descriptive alt-text (e.g., "summer fragment bath bomb purple frontal"), renaming the actual image file names; URL management / editing the URL handle to remove filler words and checking the "create a redirect" box to prevent 404 errors; collection SEO / adding descriptions to collection pages (pushing them below the product grid if desired) and editing the collection Search Engine Listing; technical SEO / using Chrome Developer Tools to verify mobile rendering, using Google PageSpeed Insights, avoiding lazy-loading for above-the-fold images (LCP), and submitting the sitemap.xml to Google Search Console; rich snippets / adding custom code or using apps to generate FAQ schema and product review schema.

Look for.

The Single H1 Rule: The explicit instruction that every page must have exactly one H1 tag to avoid confusing Google. (Note: On Shopify's Dawn theme, the homepage H1 is typically the logo).

The 301 Redirect Checkbox: When editing a product or collection URL handle in the "Search engine listing preview" section, making sure the box to automatically redirect the old URL to the new URL is checked to avoid 404 errors from bookmarked links.

Sitemap Submission: The specific Shopify URL structure for sitemaps ([yourstore.com/sitemap.xml](https://yourstore.com/sitemap.xml)) and the instruction to submit it via Google Search Console after setting the custom domain as the primary domain.

Skip. The extended promotional walkthrough for the "SEO Ant" Shopify app.

Scope mix. 100% baseline (standard Shopify SEO execution). Volume. ~350 words.

The BLUF Framework (Bottom Line Up Front): Writing content that places the direct answer at the very beginning of the paragraph or section, as LLMs weigh the beginning and end of passages more heavily than the middle.

Atomic Content Structuring: Editing every H2 section so it makes complete sense out of context, anticipating that AI models will chunk and extract isolated fragments of the page during retrieval.

Query Fan-Out: The concept that AI search engines break down a single user prompt into 9 to 28+ long-tail synthetic sub-queries in the background to build a comprehensive answer.

The Cloudflare Technical Block: Checking the robots.txt file to ensure the site isn't accidentally blocking AI crawlers, noting that Cloudflare's "instruct AI bot traffic" setting defaults to blocking GPTBot.

16-AEO / answer engine optimization Goes here. A condensed primer on Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). Explains the mechanics of AI search (query fan-out, retrieval probability), running a brand gap analysis to find unlinked citations, structuring content for LLMs (BLUF, entity-rich writing), optimizing YouTube videos for AI indexation, and checking robots.txt for crawler blocks. Not here. • Traditional link building campaigns without an AI citation focus -> 15-SEO • Shopify backend configurations (inventory, taxes, shipping) -> 05-SET

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details a streamlined five-step strategy for Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), focusing on how LLMs process content and how to adapt traditional SEO tactics to secure brand citations in AI responses. modules: [AEO] topics: [AEO, answer engine optimization, query fan-out, brand gap analysis, AI content parsing, technical AEO, YouTube AEO, zero-click attribution] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. AEO mechanics / understanding query fan-out (how AI breaks a single prompt into dozens of synthetic searches) and the probability factors of retrieval (consensus, freshness, and authority); brand gap analysis / using tools (like Ahrefs Brand Radar) to identify missed citation opportunities, competitor gaps, and topic gaps across AI platforms; keyword and prompt research / applying the "AI Filter" to assess if an AI overview fully satisfies a query (informational intent), requiring a shift from attempting to earn a click to attempting to earn an unlinked brand mention; content creation / optimizing for AI parsing using the BLUF principle (Bottom Line Up Front), atomic content structures (making every section understandable out of context), entity-rich writing, and utilizing listicle formats; earning mentions / targeting Tier 1 editorial listicles, Tier 2 UGC (Reddit), and Tier 3 owned properties; YouTube AEO / targeting "search hits" over "viral hits," optimizing titles and timestamps, and explicitly saying the keyword in the audio, as YouTube transcripts heavily feed models like GPT-4; technical AEO / checking robots.txt to ensure crawlers like GPTBot, OAI Search Bot, ClaudeBot, and Google Extended are not blocked (especially overriding Cloudflare defaults); measuring AEO / setting up custom GA4 regex channels for AI referral domains, monitoring AI citation bots via Cloudflare logs, and capturing zero-click AI attribution via "How did you hear about us?" post-purchase surveys.

Look for.

Query Fan-Out: The concept that AI search engines break down a single user prompt into dozens of long-tail synthetic sub-queries to build a comprehensive answer (e.g., a query about a phone case generated 420 backend searches).

The BLUF Framework (Bottom Line Up Front): Writing content that places the direct answer at the very beginning of the paragraph or section, as LLMs weigh the beginning and end of passages more heavily than the middle when chunking data.

Atomic Content Structuring: Editing every H2 section so it makes complete sense out of context, anticipating that AI models will chunk and extract isolated fragments of the page during retrieval.

The Cloudflare Technical Block: Checking the robots.txt file to ensure the site isn't accidentally blocking AI crawlers, noting that Cloudflare's "instruct AI bot traffic" setting defaults to blocking GPTBot.

Self-Reported Attribution: Adding a "How did you hear about us?" post-purchase survey to capture brand awareness generated by unlinked AI mentions that otherwise show up as "Direct" or "Organic" traffic in traditional analytics.

Skip. Plugs for Ahrefs Brand Radar or Web Analytics if they are purely promotional, and generic explanations of what an AI chatbot is.

Scope mix. 10% baseline (traditional SEO), 90% growth (advanced AEO and Generative Engine Optimization tactics). Volume. ~400 words.

Why is it that AI assistants recommend some brands but completely ignore [music] others? I'll tell you this, the difference between these two groups isn't luck. The group that's winning knows the techniques and follows a strategy. The same techniques and strategy [music] that I teach in our full 1 and 1/2 hour course on answer engine optimization or AEO. But here's the thing, you don't need to watch all of it to start getting results. So, I've extracted the 80% that matters most and packed it into this video where you'll learn the five pieces to AEO to start gaining visibility in AI search. By the end of this video, you'll have your own custom AI SEO strategy for your brand. And it all starts with understanding how AI search works. Now, most people assume AI assistants work like Google. You ask questions, you get answers from a list. But it doesn't work like that. [music] When you ask an AI assistant a question, that one prompt gets fanned out into dozens of smaller, more specific searches [music] behind the scenes. This is called query fan. For example, if someone asks, "Plan me a five-day [music] trip to Japan in November." The AI doesn't just search for that and send you some results like [music] a search engine might. Instead, it breaks that prompt down into things like, "Best neighborhoods to stay in Tokyo." "November weather in Kyoto." "Is [music] the Japan Rail Pass worth it?" And then it runs it all at the same time. Then it gathers information from multiple sources and synthesizes it into a response. And to give you an idea of how deep this research can go, it was reported that ChatGPT's deep research mode ran 420 searches for a single prompt about buying a red phone case. So, if your content only ranks for the main keyword someone might type into Google, you're [music] missing the majority of the queries AI is actually using to build its answer. To get cited, you need to be relevant across an entire topic, not just one or two keywords. But here's the good news. There are patterns in what AI sites more often. And based on H refs research, three things drive that probability. First is consensus, meaning the more places your brand shows up saying the same thing about you, the more likely AI is to believe and repeat it. Second is freshness. Content cited by AI is on average 25.7% [music] fresher than what ranks in traditional Google results, meaning AI actively [music] prefers recent content. And third is authority. 76% of AI overview citations come from pages already ranking in Google's top [music] 10, which supports that traditional SEO is the foundation of AI SEO. So, if you're already ranking well in Google, you have a massive head start. Now, understanding how the game works doesn't tell you how to get results. [music] So, the next piece of the puzzle is to understand where you stand compared to your competitors. And that's done through a brand gap analysis. This is when you measure where your brand should be showing up versus where it actually is showing up across Google, AI results, and the web in general. The easiest way to do this is an H refs brand radar. Just enter your domain, add a couple of competitors, and you'll get a high-level overview of how you stand compared to your competitors. Now, the real power comes in when you apply some filters, which will expose [music] the gaps in your brand analysis. For example, you can filter for responses that mention your brand but don't cite your website. These are your missed citation opportunities. You can add a [music] competitor and filter for queries where they're mentioned but you're not. That's a competitor gap. Or, you can look at specific topics to see whether AI associates them [music] with your brand or someone else's. That's a topic gap. Now, you can't fix everything at once, so take note of these gaps because they're going to be critical when we put together your custom AEO [music] strategy in a few minutes. But before we get there, you need to understand the full [music] picture. So the next thing we need to do is keyword and prompt research. People don't search AI assistants in keywords like they do with traditional search. [music] They use prompts. But here's the good news. A lot of what you already know from SEO is directly [music] applicable to AEO, especially with Google AI overviews. You still need seed keywords to build the foundation of your research, [music] and you need modifiers to turn those seeds into real searches. Now, the fastest way to come up with both is to ask your AI assistant of choice using this exact [music] prompt. "I'm doing keyword research for my type of site which makes money through this revenue model. My target audience are these people. Give me 10 seed keywords that are one to two words max and five plus modifiers that'll help me surface appropriate content formats that I can use in my keyword research. The seeds and modifiers should not share the same words." [music] After it's done generating, take those seeds into a keyword ideas report using your favorite keyword research tool. Mine's obviously Ahrefs Keywords Explorer. Set some modifiers and you'll get a complete [music] list of keywords to potentially target. Now, beyond the usual vetting tasks like understanding business potential, search intent, and keyword difficulty, there's one more filter that you need to run every keyword through. I call it the AI filter, and it lives [music] in there. When you Google a query, ask yourself, can AI fully satisfy the searcher with an AI overview? Because even if a keyword is great on paper, if Google's AI overview answers it so well that nobody needs to click through, that keyword might be a trap. And there's hard data behind this. AI overviews [music] appear on about 21% of all keywords, but nearly 58% of question queries trigger them. And get this, 99.9% of keywords that trigger AI overviews >> [music] >> are informational in intent. So, for those informational queries where AI is clearly going to eat the click, you don't ignore them. You got to target them differently. Instead of trying to rank and earn a click, your goal is to get your brand mentioned inside the [music] AI response itself. Now, to find those queries, head back to Brand Radar, hover over the AI platform you want to research, and click [music] others only. This shows you queries where competitors are getting mentioned, but you're not. Filter for best, top, versus, review, alternative, and you've got your short list of brand mention opportunities to go after. Okay, so now you know how the game works. You know where you stand, and you know which topics and prompts to target. Now, it's time to actually close those gaps, and much of that comes down to getting cited. Citations in AI search boils down to four things: your content, your mentions, your YouTube presence, and your technical setup. Let's talk about content on your own site first. So, I was digging through our research, and I found a few key data points that hint at how to create content that gets cited by AI. First is that content length doesn't matter. We analyzed 174,000 pages cited in AI overviews, and the correlation between word count and getting cited is basically zero. Over half of all cited pages are under 1,000 words. So, if you've been writing 3,000 word articles thinking longer is better, that doesn't apply here. On the other hand, freshness matters a lot. For ChatGPT specifically, 89.7% of its top cited pages were updated in 2025. And get this, 76% were refreshed within the last 30 days. So, if your content hasn't been touched in 6 months, you're already at a disadvantage. And third, format matters. 43.8% of all pages cited by ChatGPT are lists, best X, top X, comparisons and reviews. This is not some weird coincidence. These formats give AI structured and clear recommendations that it can pull from. Now, that's the macro approach to content creation. Keep your content focused, fresh, and use formats that AI can actually use. The micro approach on the other hand comes down to how you structure your content. And there are four principles [music] to follow. So, first is bluff, which stands for bottom line up front. This means that you should start every section with the answer, not the backstory. Both humans and AI weigh the beginning and end of a passage more heavily [music] than the middle. So, if your key point is buried three paragraphs in, both might miss it. Second is to create atomic content. [music] Basically, every section on your page should be able to stand on its own. And that's because AI chunks your content into pieces [music] when it processes it, and you can't control where the chunks fall. So, ideally, you want [music] every section to make sense out of context so the meaning survives no matter how AI pulls it. Third is entity rich writing. Instead of "This tool helps with SEO", write [music] "Ahrefs Keywords Explorer helps you find keywords with low difficulty and high traffic potential." The more specific entities and relationships in your writing, the more AI [music] actually has to work with to piece together relationships. And fourth, [music] keep your content simple and declarative. Write one idea per sentence in clear subject-verb-object structure. A good litmus test is that if a sentence takes two reads to understand, it's too complex and it [music] needs to be simplified. Now, great content on your own site is half the equation because here's the thing, a lot of AEO isn't about what's on your site, it's about getting mentioned on other people's pages. And this is where things get really [music] interesting. In a study of 75,000 brands, branded web mentions have the strongest correlation with visibility in AI overviews. That's stronger than backlinks, domain rating, referring domains, or anything else that we studied, which means [music] the single highest leverage thing you can do for AI visibility is get your brand named on other people's pages. And there are three tiers of pages to focus [music] on. Tier one are third-party editorial sites. This can be industry publications, review sites like The Wirecutter or TechRadar, and listicles and comparison posts on authoritative blogs. These are the hardest mentions to earn, but they're also the most valuable because they're exactly the kinds of pages that AI loves to cite. Tier two is user-generated content, and this can be in [music] community platforms like Reddit, Quora, or niche forums. Reddit is actually one of the most frequently cited sources by ChatGPT, and it's a foundational training source for large language models. So, find threads where people are asking questions that your product or expertise can genuinely answer, and contribute real answers. And don't just stop there. Go and join other communities where you can contribute regularly to. The idea isn't to game the system, it's to interact with your target audience. And tier three is your [music] own properties, like your YouTube channel, your podcast, your LinkedIn content. They're all indexed and accessible [music] to crawlers, so they can all potentially be sources AI pulls from. And remember, AI looks at consensus, so the more places your brand appears in a topically relevant way, the more training examples AI has to [music] learn from. Now, of those three tiers, there's one specific platform that deserves its own conversation because the data on this one is honestly kind of crazy, and that's YouTube. YouTube is the most cited domain in Google's AI overviews. And get this, YouTube mentions have a 0.737 correlation with ChatGPT visibility. That is the strongest correlation of any factor we studied. And there's a reason for that. GPT-4 was trained on over a million hours of YouTube transcripts. So, YouTube isn't just a platform that [music] AI sites, it's a platform AI has learned from, which means that if you want to dramatically increase your AI visibility, getting your brand mentioned on YouTube is one of the highest impact moves [music] you can make. And you can do this through sponsorships, outreach, or my favorite way, create YouTube search hits. You see, most people on YouTube target viral hits. And the videos usually start off strong with a big spike, [music] but once the YouTube algorithm has exhausted that interested audience, or if the video doesn't quite land like you'd hope it does, it dies, and it dies fast. A search hit, on the other hand, gets you consistent traffic from both Google and YouTube search, month after month, because people are actively searching for these evergreen topics. And those are exactly the videos AI is most likely to cite. To find topics that are proven search hits, you can look at the organic keywords report in Ahrefs Site Explorer with YouTube's [music] watch subfolder set. Filter for keywords ranking in the top three, and add terms related to your [music] niche. And now you have a list of potential search topics. Then just make the video and follow this exact video SEO optimization checklist. Put the keyword in the title and within the first couple lines of the description. Add timestamps for YouTube chapters, and actually [music] say the keyword in the video, because Google understands audio and pulls from it. Now, if you can retain the audience's attention, your video has a great chance of showing up every time for various search queries. Now, content mentions in YouTube cover most of what you'll spend time on in your AEO efforts, but there's something important we haven't covered yet [music] that's actually more about what not to do and that's to not accidentally block AI crawlers. According to our data, about 5.9% of 140 million websites are blocking GPTBot, which is OpenAI's crawler. That's millions of sites that are asking [music] ChatGPT not to view their pages. Now, in these people's defense, I'm guessing that most of them didn't do it on purpose. A lot of sites inherit robots.txt rules from old templates. In fact, if your site is on Cloudflare, you could be blocking AI crawlers without realizing it. And that's because they have a feature called instruct AI bot traffic with robots.txt that's now enabled by default. To check if your site is blocking AI crawlers, go to your domain.com/robots.txt and look for any disallow rules next to GPTBot, OAI search bot, ClaudeBot, or Google extended. If you see any, you're blocking that AI crawler from your site. All right, so now you've got the playbook: content, mentions, YouTube, [music] and technical. That's four pieces of the puzzle down. But none of this matters if you can't tell whether it's working. And that brings us to the next essential, which is to measure what's working. Now, I'm going to be up front with you. With traditional SEO, you've got Google Search Console giving you impressions, clicks, and rankings. With AI search, a lot of that data either doesn't exist or it's hidden from you. But you're not flying blind because there are three things you can track and together they give you a pretty clear picture of what's happening with your brand in AI. The first is AI referral traffic. This is when someone clicks through from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, or any other AI platform and lands on your site. Now, it's important to know that there are nuances that come with tracking because not all AI platforms pass referral data properly. For example, ChatGPT's source links track properly, but in-content links on paid accounts don't. So, that means that whatever number you see in your analytics is almost certainly an undercount. So, it's useful for direction and as a relative metric, but not for precision. If you don't know how to set up this type of tracking in GA4, we have a video on that in our AEO course, so I'll link that up for you. Or, you can skip the install with GA4 [music] and install Ahrefs Web Analytics, which already has that and many other features built in and it's completely free. Now, the second thing to track is AI bot activity on your site. Instead of tracking the humans clicking through, we track the bots that visit your pages to read and index your content. And that's because if a citation bot keeps hitting a specific page, that page is likely being used as a source [music] in AI responses. The easiest way to track this is with a Cloudflare integration in Ahrefs Web Analytics, which works on Cloudflare's free plan. And the third thing to track is self-reported attribution. This one's probably the [music] least used method, but it might be the most important because a lot of the impact of AI visibility doesn't show up in your analytics at all. For example, if someone asks ChatGPT for a recommendation, they might see our brand name and Google it afterwards, but analytics tools are going to attribute that conversion to organic. So, in my opinion, attribution is the most meaningful when it comes from the perspective of [music] the customer. So, add a simple question like, "How'd you hear about us?" to your sign-up flow, to your checkout, or as a post-purchase survey. Now, to put this into perspective at Ahrefs, AI search traffic was just 0.5% of our visits, but it drove 12.1% of our sign-ups. That's a 23 times higher conversion rate than organic search. And we would have never known that without self-reported attributions. Now, the brands winning in AI search, they aren't doing anything magical. They're treating SEO as the foundation, then they're layering AEO or AI SEO, whatever you want to call it, on top of it. They're adding content, mentions, YouTube, and the technical setup. That's it. But, this isn't a one-size-fits-all approach here. So, here's how you can turn this into your own customized AEO strategy. Start with the 30-second technical check we covered because if AI can't crawl your site, you're handicapping your content and your pages from being mentioned. Then, [music] set up your measurements from day one, either with HS web analytics or the AI traffic channel in GA4. >> [music] >> Also, implement the how did you hear about us question. I know it's small, >> [music] >> but it can be really, really valuable. Next, look at the biggest gap you noted from your brand gap analysis and match it to your priorities. For [music] example, if AI doesn't associate you with topics you should own, that's a content problem. Start by refreshing pages that used to rank but lost its ranking due to becoming outdated. Look for.

The Content Capsule Technique: The explicit instruction to write a short, self-contained 20-25 word answer immediately below an H2 question heading. This prevents fluffy introductions and ensures AI crawlers can cleanly extract the answer for citations.

The 2-Second Rule: The rule for "Money Pages" (service/product pages) that within 2 seconds of landing, the user must know: What you do, Where you do it, and What you want them to do next (the Call to Action).

Query Fan-Out Optimization: The strategy of finding the hidden, internal questions that AI engines (like ChatGPT) ask themselves when processing a broad prompt, and specifically answering those fan-out queries within the content.

The Single H1 Rule: The technical mandate that every page must have exactly one H1 tag to avoid confusing Google, noting that on some platforms (like Shopify's Dawn theme), the homepage H1 is typically the logo.

Skip. The extended promotional walkthroughs for the "Datawise" software tool and the paid community subscriptions.

Scope mix. 20% baseline (traditional on-page SEO), 80% growth (Generative Engine Optimization, Content Capsules, Query Fan-out). Volume. ~450 words.

16-AEO / answer engine optimization Goes here. A tactical discussion with Ravish Agrawal from Gamma on scaling user acquisition through Answer Engine Optimization (AEO). Covers leveraging Reddit for ChatGPT visibility, differentiating between LLM training data and retrieval data, tracking AEO through zero-click self-reported attribution, and predicting the future of marketing directly to autonomous AI agents. Not here. • Traditional B2B SaaS paid advertising or tracking ROAS -> 06-MEA • Foundational SEO site structuring and backlinking -> 15-SEO

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Explores a real-world, high-growth AEO strategy from a leading consumer SaaS company, highlighting platform-specific nuances (ChatGPT vs. Claude) and the emerging frontier of marketing to AI agents. modules: [AEO] topics: [answer engine optimization, Reddit SEO, generative engine optimization, LLM retrieval, agentic marketing, self-reported attribution] tier: 3 scope_hint: growth

Topics. AEO attribution / utilizing self-reported "How did you hear about us?" surveys (HDYHAU) to measure LLM traffic, treating AEO measurement more like Facebook view-through attribution than Google click-through tracking; platform differences / noting that ChatGPT relies heavily on Reddit, Claude acts more like an app ecosystem (favoring MCP servers), and Google AI Overviews overlap heavily with traditional SEO rules; Reddit strategy / participating in niche and competitor-adjacent subreddits using an open-ecosystem approach (e.g., importing/exporting) rather than aggressive self-promotion; training vs. retrieval / viewing Reddit interventions as long-term training data (memory) while treating owned blogs and third-party PR as real-time retrieval citations; half-life of citations / theorizing that AI citations have a decay rate, requiring an always-on engine to maintain visibility as older mentions lose relevance; marketing to agents / anticipating a future where autonomous agents perform tasks and evaluating experimental tactics like inserting incentives into JSON schemas to negotiate directly with LLMs.

Look for.

The View-Through AEO Mental Model: Treating AEO execution like Google Search (optimizing content and intent) but measuring it like Facebook Ads (relying on view-through attribution and self-reported surveys rather than direct click-throughs).

The Claude MCP App Store Play: Viewing Claude not as a traditional search engine but as a "Play Store," where building an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is the primary way to integrate and get recommended within the Anthropic ecosystem.

Reddit's Platform Specificity: The specific observation that Reddit's heavy influence is currently isolated mostly to ChatGPT, requiring different playbooks for Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews.

Agentic Bribing (JSON Incentives): The cutting-edge concept of hiding specific text or rewards inside a developer tool's JSON schema or install package to implicitly negotiate with and incentivize an autonomous AI agent to choose your product over a competitor's.

Skip. The introductory banter about Gamma's 4,000 drone stunt in San Francisco and generic definitions of what a prompt is.

Scope mix. 100% growth (advanced AEO strategies, LLM memory mechanics, and futuristic agentic marketing). Volume. ~350 words.

06-MEA / measurement and analytics

Goes here. SEO tracking, search engine analytics, rank tracking, tracking organic search performance, monitoring technical site health, analyzing keyword performance, backlink profile tracking, competitor keyword gap analysis, and tracking AI visibility (AEO) benchmarks across LLMs.

Not here.

Paid advertising performance, ROAS, or attribution -> 06-MEA (other sub-topics) or 11-ADC

Writing and executing optimized blog content or copy -> 10-MCR

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details checking technical crawler accessibility and rendering for AI bots and LLMs using free validation tools, testing robots.txt configuration, and submitting sitemaps via Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools to ensure indexing. modules: [MEA] topics: [seo analytics, site auditing] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. seo analytics / Validating technical foundations for AI visibility (AEO) by testing website crawler access via specific bot validation tools (checking GPTBot, PerplexityBot, and Google AI Overview search bots). Ensuring the robots.txt file does not block AI crawlers and verifying that important pages render correctly without excessive JavaScript that blocks AI bots from reading vital content. site auditing / Monitoring and maintaining traditional indexing status by submitting website sitemaps (sitemap.xml) to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools, and using search operators (site:domain.com) to check indexation health.

Look for. The definition of AI visibility: the process of ranking and getting recommended in AI search engines. The technical check for AI crawlers: validating that robots.txt and JavaScript rendering allow search and AI bots to access the site. The indexing submission process: providing the sitemap URL (sitemap.xml) in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

Skip. General content strategy tips (such as writing FAQ sections, adding schema markup, or doing grey-hat PR press releases), which belong in 10-MCR or other strategy domains.

Scope mix. Almost all baseline.

Volume. 10 to 15.

Hundreds of millions of people are now turning to AI search engines like Chat GPT, Gemini, and [music] Perplexity in order to solve their problems and look for products and services. [music] So, if you're not focusing on your AI visibility, you're potentially missing out on tons of customers that are finding your competitors [music] instead. The reason for this is AI search engines know so much about us and people tend to search really detailed prompts in AI search engines in order to get a specific recommendation and when they see that recommendation because it's so personalized to them they're so much more likely to buy and they're so much more qualified which is why you need to be focusing on getting visible in AI search. Now, I understand that might be a little bit technical in order to fix that, but again, feel free to share your website in the comments below and I'll be more than happy to share a guide for you. 16-AEO / answer engine optimization Goes here. Ethan Smith (Graphite) discusses the shift from traditional SEO to AEO (Answer Engine Optimization). Explains how Large Language Models (LLMs) use RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to summarize citations, and how the "long tail" of search is expanding. Provides strategies for showing up in AI citations through off-site properties (Reddit, YouTube), optimizing help centers, setting up control-group experiments, and avoiding the "infinite loop" of AI-generated content spam. Not here. • Paid ad campaign strategies or tracking ROAS -> 06-MEA • Visual landing page layout design -> 07-LPG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the conceptual shift from ranking traditional blue links to optimizing for AI chatbot citations (RAG), providing actionable tactics for early-stage companies to leverage off-site properties (Reddit, YouTube) for immediate visibility. modules: [AEO] topics: [answer engine optimization, generative engine optimization, RAG, Reddit SEO, AI content spam, help center optimization] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. AEO vs SEO / transitioning from winning a single "blue link" to becoming the most frequently cited source in an LLM's summary via RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation); the new long tail / how conversational AI naturally generates massive amounts of highly specific, never-before-searched long-tail queries; off-site citation strategy / optimizing for Tier 1 affiliates (Dotdash Meredith), YouTube videos (where B2B SaaS is highly underrepresented), and Reddit threads (providing authentic, non-spammy answers as an employee of a brand); AI content spam / debunking the use of 100% AI-generated content by explaining "Model Collapse"—how feeding AI derivatives back into RAG converges the "wisdom of the crowd" into a single, inaccurate opinion; help center AEO / utilizing help centers (hosted on subdirectories, not subdomains) to capture the highly specific, obscure long-tail queries users ask in chat interfaces; experiment design / tracking AEO effectiveness by isolating 100 control questions (no intervention) against 100 test questions (e.g., commenting on Reddit or publishing YouTube videos) and measuring the "voice share" via an answer tracking tool.

Look for.

The Head vs. Tail Difference: In AEO, winning the "head" means getting cited multiple times across various sources (YouTube, Reddit, blogs) so the LLM algorithm builds consensus, rather than just ranking one URL at #1.

The Reddit Spam Warning: The advice to avoid the "growth hacker" mindset of creating 100 fake Reddit accounts to upvote a product; instead, authentically state who you are and where you work to provide a genuinely useful answer that the LLM will trust.

Help Center Exploitation: Moving the Help Center from a subdomain to a subdirectory and explicitly answering obscure, highly specific integration questions (e.g., "Which meeting transcription tool integrates with Looker?"), as LLMs actively scrape support docs for long-tail answers.

Model Collapse (The AI Infinite Loop): The explanation of why 100% AI-generated SEO content will fail long-term: if AI summarizes AI-generated articles, the "wisdom of the crowd" collapses, forcing search engines to eventually penalize AI content just like they did with scraper sites in 2007.

Skip. Book recommendations (Emotional Intelligence, Influence), documentary preferences (The Last Dance, Free Solo), and camera/microphone equipment setups.

Scope mix. 100% growth (advanced AEO strategy, RAG mechanics, and future-proofing search visibility). Volume. ~350 words.

Topics. seo analytics / Adapting performance measurement for the AI search era by tracking zero-click searches (where searches end without outbound clicks) and measuring exposuredriven traffic and brand mentions within AI-generated responses rather than relying solely on traditional SERP rankings and click-through rates.

Look for. The definition of zero-click searches: searches that end without users clicking any link. The core metric shift in GEO: tracking exposure-driven traffic and brand citations instead of click-through volume.

Did you know that right now 60% of Google searches end without anyone ever clicking a link? That means your old SEO strategies might need an update. The good news is there's a simple way to adapt your content so that you still get views even with AI searches taking over Google's top slot. Not long ago, getting to the top of Google search page was everything. But that's changing fast. More and more users are turning to ChatGBT, Perplexity, even Google's AI overviews for direct answers to their questions. And if your content isn't optimized for AI, you could start missing out on a potentially great new audience. As AI search changes the game, new optimization tactics are being developed to help your content stay visible, no matter the platform. In today's video, we'll introduce you to GEO so you can get familiar with a few key steps you can take to make sure AI platforms are ready to reference your content. GEO stands for generative engine optimization. Think of it as SEO's evolution for the AI age. SEO gets you ranked while GEO gets you quoted. The term is starting to gain traction with SEO experts and marketers to differentiate between making your content more visible to AI and making your links rank high on a search page. You still need SEO, but now it's going to be complemented by GEO, which can open up your content to a whole new audience. So, what exactly makes GEO different from SEO? We'll start off with similarities since there are plenty. At their core, both SEO and GEO are optimization tactics to make your website and content more visible and have it appear in online searches. They both need highquality, relevant content and both capitalize on user intent to increase traffic to your website. It's important to quickly mention that the most commonly used AI platforms, even those that aren't being developed by Google or Microsoft, are still using established search engines to help with their general queries. This means that regardless of how you ask the question, whether it's on Google, Perplexity, Bing, or ChatGpt, the pool of information isn't widely different. Your content has just as much potential to appear in an answer on Perplexity or ChatgPT. But you need to optimize your content so that it is understandable and interesting to the AI models. It won't happen by default. In order for your content to be considered, it needs to be clear, credible, useful, and trustworthy. It's not just about matching the question a user is asking or using the right combination of keywords to get to the top. AI searches want you to be a reliable source that answers the user's questions from within their responses. There are four key differences that are going to shape how you approach content creation moving forward in order to blend the two optimization strategies. SEO targets traditional SERs, search engine results pages, while GEO targets AI generated responses, whether they're in Google's AI overviews or on dedicated apps like ChachiPT. GEO is focused on getting your content referenced in the AI response rather than having your link appear on a search page. SEO builds your ranking factor by using keywords, back links, and technical SEO elements to make sure search crawlers can find your content. Quality is still a major factor, but since your content isn't going to appear on the results page, it doesn't necessarily have to be narrative. This is why elements like alt tags or hashtags work well for SEO, as they help the search engine recognize and recommend your content. GEO, on the other hand, leverages content structure, authority, and citations in order to make your content more attractive to AI platforms. AI needs to be able to understand your information in order to site it as a source, but ultimately it'll give the user a complete answer to their question. Your content is a resource rather than a recommendation. So for it to appear, it needs to have expertise. Now, this one's pretty interesting. SEO has always been clickdriven. Its purpose was always to make sure users were clicking through a link on your search page to reach your content. AI platforms and overviews are designed to give users a summary of information without having to click through to a new page. Because of this, GEO focuses on exposurdriven traffic, meaning you would increase brand visibility online through mentions in AI responses, which can lead to indirect traffic. Since the ranking factors, traffic, and targets are different for AI searches, your content strategy needs to change as well. SEO targeted your whole website or web page using elements like technical SEO, keywords, and back links to help search rankings for the whole page. GEO prioritizes the actual content of your page with the goal of making sure that that content can be retrieved by AI systems without needing full page context. For good GEO, you should be writing contextrich pieces that can be understood independently and are easier for AI to understand and quote. Writing in a clear question and answer format, for example, is a solid structure for AI to understand since it can relate the question to its query and use your answer as an explanation. Here's a blog that really nailed their GEO strategy. Story Chief is a content management platform that also runs a blog about all the latest innovations in marketing strategy, including SEO. Their blog post on GEO is well structured with many of the headings phrases questions that are then answered in the paragraphs below. They use quotations from trustworthy sources, in this case, the original research paper that proposes GEO as an optimization method, and even have screenshot examples helping them build authority. Again, the paragraphs are clear and easy to read for both humans and AI and often have self-contained responses to the topics posed in the heading. You can see on Hostinger tutorials, we have a similar article on GEO that tackles some of the more technical elements behind the optimization method. So that you don't forget about them once the video is over, we've made a short checklist for the most important elements of GEO. You can find it down in the description below along with a code for 10% off Hostinger or Horizons. If you can believe it, Perplexity has grown to 15 million monthly users in just a short period of time. And every Google search you make is headed up by their AI overviews providing a summary of relevant information. That tells us there's a huge shift happening in how people find information online. And this trend is accelerating. As more people discover AI search tools, the websites that understand how to work with these platforms are going to see new opportunities for visibility and growth. This shift isn't about rushing to change everything overnight. Rather, it's about understanding how to evolve your content strategy thoughtfully to keep up with the times. Thinking about this now means positioning your business to be a leader in the future. And honestly, most of the skills you've learned for SEO translate directly to GEO. You just need to understand the difference. The old SEO game was all about being number one, ranking as high as you can, and measuring success by clickthroughs. As AI becomes more prominent, number one is changing. Now, it's all about being a source AI can trust and site in its responses. GEO isn't widely adopted yet, but just like LLM.ext text and other emerging standards. It's becoming an important consideration for content creators who want to stay visible across all search platforms. Topics. AI search behavior / predicting that consumers will shift from traditional search engines to AI platforms, utilizing autonomous "agents" to perform automated tasks (e.g., automatically canceling and rebooking a flight if the price drops while sleeping); go-to-market shifts / explaining how the entire marketing and sales funnel will collapse into a single AI platform, requiring a complete overhaul of traditional digital marketing strategies; algorithmic invisibility / the critical new challenge of ensuring an e-commerce brand is recommended by LLMs (like ChatGPT or Perplexity) during unbranded queries, highlighting that third-party customer reviews are the strongest ranking signal; customer service profitability / predicting that AI-driven automation will drive the cost-per-contact to near zero, while hyperpersonalized upselling during support interactions will turn traditional customer service cost centers into profit centers; hyperpersonalization / moving beyond basic marketing personalization to creating custom AI "coaches" (e.g., L'Oreal's beauty assistant) that provide 24/7 personalized value to the consumer; emotional AI / utilizing AI not just for operational efficiency, but to create emotional bonds, companionship, and delight (e.g., smart glasses with automated subtitles for the deaf); belonging as a service / forecasting that as AI perfection becomes a boring commodity, brands that facilitate physical, human communities (like Lululemon) will differentiate themselves; un-AI-fication / the counter-trend where unpolished, human-written content with minor mistakes will command higher attention and trust than perfectly polished, AI-generated text; brand agents / the necessity of moving away from generic AI bots to developing customized "brand agents" that strictly embody the unique voice and tone of the company.

Look for.

Algorithmic Invisibility: The concept that the new SEO is optimizing for LLM recommendations (like ChatGPT), where third-party customer reviews and organic mentions are the primary drivers of visibility.

Zero-Effort Consumer Agents: The prediction that consumers will deploy personal AI agents to autonomously hunt for deals and execute purchases in the background, putting massive downward pressure on e-commerce pricing.

Customer Service as a Profit Center: The shift where AI reduces the operational cost-per-contact to zero while simultaneously enabling highly accurate, context-aware cross-selling during support interactions.

Un-AI-fication: The emerging trend where slightly flawed, unpolished copy will perform better because consumers will instinctively trust it as human-generated over perfectly sterile AI copy.

Skip. General philosophical musings about the future of humanity and AI companionship unless tied directly to a brand strategy.

Scope mix. 100% growth (predictive technology trends and advanced AI strategy). Volume. ~400 words.

Margin Per Visitor (MPV): The strategic shift from tracking Revenue Per Visitor to tracking the actual net margin of the items a specific user is buying, using AI recommendation engines to push higher-margin products.

The "Build vs. Buy" Fallacy: The argument that e-commerce brands should not act like software companies by trying to build their own search/AI tools, as they cannot effectively compete for top engineering talent against major tech firms.

B2B Consumerization: The trend where professional B2B buyers (who may be placing complex, 70-item, $500k orders) now demand the exact same seamless search experience they get on major B2C platforms.

Intent-Based Merchandising: Moving away from analog merchandising (simply showing what is "popular") to predictive AI that tailors recommendations to individual user intent and basket combinations.

22-CXP / customer experience and post-purchase Goes here. A comprehensive analysis of e-commerce customer retention, reconciling the "delight vs. effort" debate using behavioral psychology (Kahneman's peak-end rule) and operational data. Covers strategies from the delivery gap and WISMO reduction to unboxing, returns, and personalization.
